column2: “On the contrary, Socrates, it certainly is,” Polemarchus cut in, “if we’re to put any trust in Simonides.”
column3: 331d. Polemarchus opposes Socrates’ negative conclusion and defends returning what is owed.

column2: “Then I’m your heir, aren’t I?” said Polemarchus.
column3: 331d. Burnet’s Greek makes Polemarchus the speaker and the first-person heir, setting up Socrates’ reply at 331e. Shorey confirms.

column2: “Now picture people walking behind that wall. They carry all sorts of things that stick up above it, including human figures and animals made of stone, wood and other materials. As you’d expect, some of the people carrying them talk and others keep quiet.”
column3: 514c–515a. Restores explicit human figures (ἀνδριάντας) alongside the animal figures in the cave.
